correctness.rationale: For every connected girth>=6 finite source graph G with at least one edge, the centered ball core B collapses by unique-connector free pairs to Cl(L(G))~G. A Rips simplex outside B must contain three pairwise disjoint source edges whose three unique connectors alternate around a simple hexagon; the sixth-cycle reconstruction is injective. An extra compatible source edge cannot touch an alternating edge or be disjoint from all three: either yields a 3-, 4- or 5-cycle by connector restrictions/pigeonhole; thus exactly two maximal exceptional triangles per hexagon EVEN WHEN hexagons overlap. Their boundary loops are the original graph six-cycles; attaching one cell for each and then a second homotopic cell yields K~X(G) vee (vee^h S^2). Cellular boundary image is hexagon lattice rank r, so H1 is its quotient, H2 free rank 2h-r and no higher homology; possible H1 torsion is explicitly retained. The source verifier constructs centered/Rips complexes, replays collapses, and tests overlapping theta graphs, subdivisions of complete graphs and Heawood. Finite mod-two tests are only corroboration.
